question.prompt:
In \(\triangle ABC\), \(AB=AC\), \(\angle A=36^\circ\), and \(BD\) bisects \(\angle ABC\), intersecting \(AC\) at \(D\). Among \(\triangle ABC\), \(\triangle ABD\), and \(\triangle BCD\), how many are isosceles triangles? (Enter a number.)

[Figure 1](figures/cnm_138_q5_question_en.svg)

solutions.explanation: \(\angle ABC=\angle C=72^\circ\), and \(\angle ABD=36^\circ=\angle A\), so \(DA=DB\). Also, \(\angle BDC=72^\circ=\angle C\), so \(BD=BC\). All three triangles are isosceles triangles.
solutions.title: Equal angles give equal sides
